newsitem.title: UK: Milupa confirms UK baby milk withdrawal.
newsitem.headline: Milupa confirms UK baby milk withdrawal.

text.p: Milupa, a subsidiary of Dutch specialist food producer NV Verenigde Bedrijven Nutricia, confirmed on Friday it was withdrawing its Milumil baby milk powder in Britain.
A spokeswoman said Britain's health department suspected salmonella contamination. She could not yet tell how many Milumil packs would be have to be withdrawn.
Shares in Nutricia dropped 16.20 guilders ($8.80) to 260.50 before the Amsterdam Stock Exchange suspended trading. Milumil commands about nine percent of the British powdered milk market.
In a statement, the health department said no other Milupa milks than Milumil, which is produced in France, were affected.

"Parent and carers of children are advised to discontinue use of Milumil immediately," the ministry said after it was informed there was a link between infection with "Salmonella anatum" and prior consumption of Milumil.
The Public Health Laboratory Service identified 12 such infections with children under the age of 12 months. Two children were admitted to hospital and have now recovered. ($1=1.840 Guilder)
